title: Coming in the next release
added: Replay of past traffic on the live map, built into the portal: play any past time from the hub's own history at 1x to 100x, step by minutes, pick a date and time (in the site's time zone), and share a link to a moment; key Y

Heat map of past traffic on the live map: any period up to the longest range in Settings, ending now or in the past, drawn from the hub's history on a grid that follows the zoom, with the altitude limits, strength and spread, and its own legend

Settings > Public Pages: Replay and Heatmap (the portal's own or the classic tar1090 pages), the speed and start time of the Replay, how much history each worker keeps ready, the most heat squares per request

Live map: select several aircraft at once (key M, click each; key T selects all shown, Esc deselects), each with its own track and in the link you copy; persistence (key P) keeps aircraft that stop being heard on the map, dimmed, for the time set in Settings

ACARS: members' ACARS, VDL Mode 2 and HF datalink receivers send their messages (through a small bridge program) to a private address on the site; the ACARS page lists them with filters, a chart and a station page for each receiver, an aircraft's card on the live map shows its latest messages, and members add their stations on My ACARS Stations (administrators add one for a member, switch stations off and hide an aircraft on request). It is a new service container (acars) with its own database, switched on in Settings > ACARS

Repeater Code Plug Export: pick repeaters by band, mode, place, distance and status and download them as the Anytone DM32's channel and talkgroup lists (a DMR repeater becomes one channel per talkgroup), a CHIRP file, or an RT Systems style file; the page lists what goes in each DM32 field
Admin > Repeaters: a queue of repeaters waiting for a position (those brought in from a radio), with the place their city names offered in one click

Mesh nodes: Meshtastic nodes that publish themselves (the map report a node sends on purpose) and MeshCore nodes that advertise (heard by an observer, signature checked) are listed, mapped and given a page, with the gateways and observers that heard each and the signal (who hears whom), a network filter, and links to the Arkansas and nearby meshes. It is a new service (mesh, with our own Mosquitto broker and its own database) switched on in Settings > Mesh Nodes

My Mesh Nodes: every member makes their own broker login (its own username and a long random password) for a node or an observer computer, with the Meshtastic and MeshCore settings filled in; it can publish and read nothing, and can be changed, switched off or deleted without touching anyone else's. Administrators make one for a member, switch off, delete and sync. Only the certificate and a router forward of TCP 8883 are left to the administrator
Full screen on every map: a button on the map's top right corner (Esc leaves it)

Radiosonde stations can send frames directly: a claimed station makes a private upload address on My Radiosonde Stations and a small bridge program passes on auto_rx's payload summary (a station already uploading to SondeHub needs nothing more)

Mesh nodes: the broker finds its TLS certificate in the proxy's certificate store and follows renewals by itself; the public Meshtastic server's Arkansas topic can also be read (Settings > Mesh Nodes)

Admin > Usage: every request the site makes to outside services counted by host (today, 7 and 30 days, failures, data read), the stored data of every service and the portal's own database, and the live feeds

Radiosonde predictions: three predictors to pick from on a launch site's Forecast block (past flights, our own forecast-wind flight model, and Tawhiri once an address is set), each scored against real landings; forecast winds are asked for sparingly (kept 6 hours, limited per day)
Live map: Without position only filter (key G) for aircraft that are heard but send no position; Display menu: show all times in UTC
Live map: an ACARS positions layer shows aircraft out of ADS-B range that reported a position by ACARS, ADS-C or HFDL, dimmed with the age of the report (Settings > ACARS sets how long)

Mesh Map: measured coverage of gateways and observers (the farthest node each was heard to hear in each direction, labelled as measured, not predicted); Mesh Health page: routers gone quiet, low batteries, busy channels, old firmware and places a router is missing

Mesh nodes can be claimed: put a code in the node's name and it becomes yours (or an administrator approves); you choose whether your name shows as its operator and can hide the node from the mesh pages
Live map: altitude can be corrected for air pressure (the QNH the aircraft sends, or one you type) and the map can select an aircraft by itself for a wall display (key A)
All My Stations: one page with a card for everything you run (ADS-B feeders, weather, radiosonde, ACARS, repeaters, mesh) and a count for each

Repeaters: linked systems. Groups of repeaters linked together show as a badge on the list (which can be filtered by system), as a Linked Repeaters section on each repeater's page, and as lines between them on the Repeater Map; administrators and repeater owners make and change them

Site themes: color schemes (Midnight, Ocean, Forest, Sunset, Slate, High Contrast, Paper, Daylight) and seasonal and holiday themes (spring, summer, fall, winter, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year, Independence Day, Easter, St. Patrick's Day, Valentine's Day) that switch on by date, with drifting decorations and their own symbols on the maps (Santa on some aircraft at Christmas, pumpkins and skeletons on the balloons at Halloween). Pick any in the Display menu; a Normal Look button goes back at once when the site puts a seasonal theme on; administrators set the dates in Admin > Themes
improved: Weather map: wind streams follow a smooth wind field and curve instead of running in straight lines when zoomed out
Weather map: a new region opens at once with what is kept and fills in as airport weather arrives
Radiosonde Statistics: the bar charts are the shared hover charts with grid and labelled axes
Weather map: the heat map has its own color bar and legend section when it shows a different reading than the labels
Radiosonde Station Coverage runs by itself at the first pass after an update when it has never run
Call sign details (name, class, place) on hover in the Radiosonde Map receiving station card and on APRS stations in the Weather Map card and popups
Repeater Map: call sign and frequency labels (a setting), and Radiosonde Map: balloon, receiving station and launch site labels now come from one label engine, so no two labels ever overlap
The menu's Heatmap and Replay now open the portal's own on the live map; the classic tar1090 pages remain under Classic Map (or ?classic=1)

Maps: the Map selector switches between Aircraft, Weather Stations, Radiosondes, Counties, Coverage, Repeaters and APRS Stations in place, without reloading the page; the view stays, and the address, title, menu and Back button follow

Labels never overlap on any map: the live map's aircraft labels and the County Map's labels join the APRS, Repeater and Radiosonde maps on one shared label engine (the most important label wins a crowded spot; the weather map's labels still combine into averages, now with the same engine), and it measures each label as drawn
The How to Feed pages all list the other feeding pages, now including Radiosondes, ACARS and Mesh Nodes; the new ACARS and Mesh pages follow the same form as the others
Radiosonde Flights: a Heard by list filters the flights by receiving station
Radiosonde Flights: Heard by is a box you type in, with the receiving stations to pick from

Upload addresses and servers on the weather, ACARS, radiosonde and mesh pages use the Feed Hostname (feed.arksignal.allisononline.org), so feeds can move to more hosts later; older addresses keep working

Mesh nodes: Arkansas nodes already uplinking to Meshtastic's public server appear without doing anything (the public server's Arkansas topic is read by default; switch it off in Settings > Mesh Nodes)
Radiosonde Map: Show These Flights becomes Hide These Flights once the history is shown
Radiosonde Map: forecast flights are numbered in the order they launch
SondeHub is credited on every radiosonde page and in the map credits of every map that shows its data (balloons, receiving stations, forecasts)
fixed: Receiving stations with a slash in the call sign (KFS/SE) have a one-segment address (KFS~SE); the old address redirects
A restore could fail with a deadlock while the flight log was being written; the flight log recorder and restores now take turns
Radiosonde Map: a launch forecast can be cleared (Clear Forecast on the launch site, Clear Forecasts on the map)

title: Radio overview, repeater positions, background service status, Grafana filters, one-segment station links
added: Radio overview page and a separate Repeater List with a Location column
Set or correct a repeater's position on its page: click or drag on a map, or search an address
Bullseye button on every map to show where you are, and Drive Times From My Location
Show on Map goes to the map of its own kind (a weather station to the Weather Map, a hospital to the County Map)
improved: Show my location no longer zooms the map when it opens
Service Status opens at once and shows the result of background checks that run on a schedule; only an administrator can force a run
Coverage Map opens on Arkansas with only the ADS-B coverage on; radiosonde stations show as antennas with their coverage outline
Weather Statistics shows the main readings as two columns of charts
Grafana: the Weather Dashboard and Radiosonde Dashboard carry the filters (renamed from Balloon Statistics)
The home page note about services still to come is built from the roadmap
Station addresses with a slash in the call sign (APRS repeaters) use a tilde and always work
fixed: Weather Statistics said the statistics could not be loaded
APRS repeater links such as 147.090/R gave a 404
Frequencies page wording: FRS needs no license, GMRS needs one

A backup restore could fail with a deadlock if it ran at the same moment as a background update; a restore now waits for the weather statistics and data updates to finish and keeps them out until it is done

title: Weather for any place, DMR and call sign tools, one-engine maps, Grafana statistics, frequencies
added: Satellite and Hybrid (satellite with roads and place names) map styles on every map, from Display and View
Show my location on every map (your browser's position stays in your browser)
County Map: a plain outline that needs no data or shading
Radiosonde flight page: search and filters on the Heard By table, and the details say who heard it last, how many stations heard it, the best signal and the farthest listener
Settings > Map Tiles and Weather > Map Sections By Map Type: choose which map types show which Layers and Filters sections (Drive Times now only on the County and Aircraft maps)

Weather Map: bring in the APRS weather stations and airport weather in the same format as the members' stations (an airport APRS also carries is drawn once, as airport weather), with a Hide airport weather filter on the APRS pages and map
Weather Map: a heat map of the reading shown and wind streams across the whole map, worked out from every station switched on; cloud cover from airport weather is a new reading

Repeaters: DMR ID, talkgroups by time slot, and the settings of D-STAR, Fusion, P25 and NXDN on a repeater's page and in its edit form; an editor can import a radio's code plug (the DM32's channel list) to add color codes, talkgroups and tones; call sign lookup of the licensee (name, class, status, expiry, city)
Weather Statistics: chart and tabulate every weather source (members, APRS, airports) and filter by source, county, city, ZIP code, station and period

Radiosonde Statistics: search by flight, receiving station or launch site; filter by kind, status and dates; flights per day, how high they burst, typical flight time and which stations heard the most
Radiosonde Map: click a launch site for its past flights between two dates, the forecast flights of its next launches, and a forecast for a launch at a date and time you pick
Coverage Map: limit any layer to one or more counties, cities or ZIP codes
Profile: each My page (My Feeders, My Weather Stations, My Sonde Stations) lists your stations and has its Claim or Add form on the same page, no separate menu entries

Weather for a Place: type a ZIP code, city, airport or address and get a full weather page made from the stations near it (current conditions, National Weather Service forecast, history charts, the stations used)
Call Sign Lookup page: a US call sign's FCC license record (through Callook.info) with FCC and QRZ links and what the site knows about it
County outlines: a box on every map (except the County Map) draws a thin line around every county
Weather maps: heat map and wind streams are two boxes that can be on together, and the heat map can show a different reading than the labels
DMR talkgroup and contact lists: import a radio's exported lists (or RadioID-style and BrandMeister-style lists); a scheduled update can read them from addresses you set once you have permission

Grafana: Weather Statistics and Radiosonde Statistics dashboards with filters (sources, reading, period, counties, cities, ZIP codes, stations; kinds, launch sites, receiving stations, flights) read the portal's public statistics, delivered by the normal update (no database login on the hub)
Weather for a Place, call sign info wherever a call sign appears, DMR time slots and talkgroups on repeaters with standard talkgroups, a combined Call Signs, Contacts and Talkgroups page
County Map: Outline only, like the other maps (a thin line around every county and nothing else)
Frequencies page (Radio menu): APRS, calling frequencies, FRS, GMRS, MURS, weather radio, marine and Meshtastic in one searchable list that editors can add to
improved: Balloon Map: a balloon launched from a known launch site no longer gets a launch flag on top of the site's icon
Admin: Radiosondes and Hospitals are split into tabs; the Coverage Map uses the same map layout as every other map
Clicking a label on a map does the same as clicking the aircraft, station or county it belongs to
Balloon Map: a Show Balloons choice (All, Live only, Landed only) replaces In the air now only; forecast flights start exactly at their launch site
Balloon Map: live windows stop at 48 hours; for older flights pick From and To dates to load history

Show on Map buttons (balloon flight, launch site, receiving station, aircraft, APRS station, county, airport, hospital, weather station) now show only that item; clear the chip to see everything again
The details card on every map can be collapsed to its title bar; on a phone, opening it folds Layers and Filters away so the two never cover the map
Radiosonde Map: every marker (balloon, launch, burst, landing, launch site, receiving station) opens the same flyout; tracks are brighter and thicker; forecast flights start switched off
Renamed: Radiosonde Map, Sonde Receiving Stations, My Sonde Stations; the Aircraft and ADS-B feeder statistics are in the Aircraft menu
Airline logos are served from memory with a validator, so a busy map asks the database far less
Radiosonde Map: Show Balloons choices and every marker opens the flyout (see above); Weather Map sources and Show Airport duplicates are handled once
ADS-B Feeders is in the Aircraft menu with the other aircraft pages (Network keeps the coverage and status pages)
A balloon on the Aircraft Map opens its details in a popup instead of leaving the page
Show my location explains why it cannot work on an address that is not https, instead of silently unticking

Weather maps combine labels that would overlap when zoomed out into one label with the average of their readings and a count; click it to zoom in (Settings > Weather Stations sets how close and how far in)
Radiosonde station coverage on the Coverage Map is drawn like the ADS-B coverage: each station its own color and an outline of how far it heard a balloon in every direction
Layers and Filters fold away whenever a balloon, launch site, station or any other item is picked, on every screen size

Weather map: stations load for the view only and for any region; labels never overlap; the heat map and wind streams sit under the markers; charts match the radiosonde flight page; radiosonde station coverage is built from the flights each station really heard
APRS Map: station labels never overlap (weather stations first); a label that would overlap another is left off until you zoom in
Weather for a Place: forecast cards have weather icons and rain chance; stations used are limited to 12 miles unless fewer than two are reporting
Call Sign Lookup lists everything the site knows: repeaters with DMR IDs and color codes, contact-list DMR IDs (members), APRS stations, feeders, weather and sonde stations
Weather for a Place opens on your location and has Use My Location; its charts (and the station and flight page charts) are two columns on a wide screen
Drive times fold Layers and Filters away on every map, the same as picking an item
Feeders are airplane badges on the Feeders page and the Coverage Map, easy to see at state level
Admin: every section starts collapsed, and a form that reloads a page keeps where you were scrolled to and which sections were open
Repeaters imported from a radio's code plug are approved at once (listed, but not on the map until given a position)
Popups on every map (the Coverage Map's stations too) fold Layers and Filters, like picking an item
Call Sign page and the DMR contacts search link to RadioID.net for a person's DMR ID
DMR contacts list the call sign, sort and filter, and Call Sign Lookup finds DMR IDs by call sign (re-import the contact file once)
Weather map: the heat map draws in passes from coarse to fine and wind streams cover the whole map whatever the heat map shows
fixed: An amateur balloon that went up near a weather-service launch site was shown as launched from that site and marked NWS; amateur balloons have no launch site and are never NWS
Show on Radiosonde Map for a flight far from Arkansas opened on Arkansas instead of the flight (the opening zoom animation finished over the move)
The Submissions Waiting link in Admin > Repeaters gave an internal server error for a repeater without a position
Wind streams only covered the area of the stations that had the heat map's reading

DMR contact lists whose first column is a row number (ID) with the real DMR ID in a DMR ID column and a Call Sign column are read correctly; several lists can be imported at once and replace the old ones
security: Updated Werkzeug to 3.1.9 (a published vulnerability in 3.1.8)

title: One map layout, admin by service with setting search, APRS lists and map labels
added: County Map: show counties shaded, outlined, or both, and switch back and forth
Every map has a Map selector at the top that switches between the kinds of map (aircraft, weather stations, balloons, counties, repeaters, APRS) and keeps your view

Admin: the menu is organized by service (Aircraft and Feeders, Weather and Balloons, Radio, Map and Data, Updates, Site), each with its own Settings page; a search box on every admin page finds any setting and opens it
improved: Radio overview: click a column heading to sort, like the other lists
APRS Stations and APRS Weather: search box and click-to-sort headings
APRS Map: station labels with the weather reading of your choice (in your own units), like the other maps
Maps: opening the Legend now folds away Layers and Filters instead of stacking under it; the button is called Layers & Filters
The aircraft map and the Weather Map are built on the same map layout as the other maps, so panels, the Legend, the fold arrow and Drive Times behave the same everywhere
fixed: APRS Weather and other server-built pages follow the units you choose in the Display menu even when you are signed out (the browser's choice is now remembered in a cookie)

title: Drive times from anywhere, one location precision list
added: Service Status has a row for the routing server (OSRM) behind the hospital drive-time rings

Drive times from anywhere: switch on Click the map to pick a place and press Show Drive Times From Here (or search a city or an address and choose Drive times from ...) and the nearest hospitals are listed by road drive time and road distance, ties and near-ties by trauma level and services, with rings of 15, 30, 60 and 90 minutes (an estimate, not an ambulance's route)

County Map: drive-time rings only when you ask (a hospital's popup, or the Hospital Drive-Time Rings choice for the Level I and II or all trauma centers), thick colored lines with minute labels, now including a 90 minute ring

Location precision: one list of twelve steps (Exact down to 40 feet, then 400 feet, a quarter mile, 0.7 mile, 1.5 miles, 3 miles, the site's General, 15, 30 and 60 miles, Hidden) for feeders, weather stations, radiosonde stations and the administrator defaults, written in your own units
Admin > Full Roadmap shows everything; the public Roadmap shows only what is meant for the public
improved: Long pages have a round arrow at the bottom right that takes you back to the top
Data Updates: the page shows what is running; different sources can run at the same time, but a source cannot start while it, or one whose data it uses (or that uses its data), is running

Airline logos: the map no longer waits for logos to be fetched (they are fetched in the background and kept, and logos for the airlines in the air are fetched ahead of time), so the aircraft map loads quickly with logos on
Balloon Map and Flights page: shorter windows of 1, 2 and 3 hours
MLAT Network page: the station dots are bigger, with a halo and a white edge
Radiosondes: receiving stations are shown to about 0.7 mile until their owner chooses (it was General, about 6 miles)
Picking a place, airport or hospital in a map's search clears the search box so nothing stays filtered, flies there and marks it with a label for a few seconds
fixed: The routing server address default is the one the hub and production reach (172.16.254.101); 1.1.0 shipped the WireGuard tunnel address
APRS Weather: pressure shows two decimals in inches of mercury

title: Balloon forecasts and history, repeaters, APRS, highways, drive-time rings, one search and saved views, and a phone-friendly site
added: Balloon forecast flights: for each upcoming launch the Balloon Map draws where it will launch from, its path (colored by height), where it will burst and where it will land, shaped like past flights from the same site, season and hour and pulled toward the latest flights; a separate switch shows the area half of such flights landed in

Historical balloon flights: every flight SondeHub's archive holds for the Little Rock launch site and the sites around Arkansas can be brought in as full flights, slowly in the background (switch it on under Admin > Radiosondes > Historical Flights)
Repeaters: also adds the repeaters APRS stations announce, and administrators can import a list a club or council gave permission to use (a CSV file)

The Radiosondes overview lists Arkansas only by default (flights launched in Arkansas, the receiving stations and launch sites there); Settings > Radiosondes > Radiosondes Overview Shows adds Missouri, Tennessee, Mississippi, Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma or anywhere else. The Balloon Map and All Flights still show every state
Display menu: Distances in settings (site default, feet and miles, or metres and kilometres), saved with your account
improved: In progress: predictions for future balloon flights, the SondeHub archive and a prediction service

Radiosonde settings that were in kilometers and meters (launch site match distance, landed-below altitude, recovery radius) are now distance settings shown in feet and miles, or in your own choice of units

Phones: the menu opens full screen with one group open at a time and whole-row taps; the section bar opens over the page instead of pushing it down; tables turn into cards; the home map's layer list starts folded; the Coverage Map fits a phone; the footer stays at the bottom on short pages; scrolling is smoother (the page background no longer repaints while you scroll, and blur effects are off on touch screens)
County Map: a Highlight and Name on Hover switch, off by default (Settings > Counties sets the site default)

Maps: one search box on every map finds airports, places, hospitals, repeaters, APRS stations, balloons and counties and flies there; Saved Views remember where a map is looking, its filters and its layers (kept with your account when signed in)
Highways: a map layer of the Interstates, US highways and state highways (from the Census, kept on this site) on every map with the Layers list
Hospital pages: drive-time rings show how far a vehicle gets in 15, 30 and 60 minutes by road (our own estimate from the network's routing server, not an ambulance's route); worked out once and kept

APRS: stations, digipeaters, gateways and weather stations (including Citizen Weather Observer Program stations) read from the amateur radio APRS-IS network around Arkansas, with a list, a map, a page for each station, an APRS Weather page in your own units, a takedown list for call signs, and an APRS service of its own (own container and database)

Repeater directory: amateur radio repeaters, linked nodes and gateways in every mode (FM, DMR, D-STAR, Fusion, P25) from Hearham's open listing and Arkansas hams, with a list and filters, a page for each repeater, a Repeater Map, reports of problems, sysop claims, member submissions that wait for an editor and a Radio menu; the search box finds a frequency or call sign

Balloon landing forecasts: a new prediction service (its own container and database) imports SondeHub's open archive back to 2022 for Arkansas and the surrounding launch sites and forecasts where the balloons of upcoming launches will land, from past flights of the same site, season and hour and the latest winds; every forecast is scored against the real flight. See Next Launch Forecast on the Radiosondes page and Forecast landing areas on the Balloon Map
Load a Flight by Serial: signed-in members can pull any flight from SondeHub's public archive by serial (Balloon Flights page); it is kept here like any other flight
Radiosonde predictions: the whole predicted path to the landing is kept and drawn on the flight page and the map, not just a line to the landing point
The faint range labels on the page background and the radar, the privacy-precision wording, the live map altitude legend and filters now follow your units too

One units choice for the whole site: imperial (feet, mph, miles, degrees F) by default, set per person in the Display menu (imperial, aeronautical or metric) and saved with the account; the aircraft and balloon maps, the balloon flight page and charts, range statistics, airports, flight history, weather and every distance in Admin settings follow it. The site default is Settings > Units (Site Default)
Every map now has the small arrow at the bottom of its open panels that folds them away (the Balloon Map, Weather Map, County Map, Repeater Map and APRS Map were missing it)
fixed: The balloon map and the aircraft map's balloon layer draw a flight's whole track, from launch to landing, thinned evenly; before, a long flight showed only its last hour or so

Weather stations that are not reporting no longer appear on the aircraft map (Settings > Weather Stations > Hide Offline Stations on the Aircraft Map; a visitor can switch it with Reporting Now Only in the Weather panel)

title: Balloon recovery reports and chase mode, folding home card, and a setting for where each map opens
added: Balloon recovery reports: signed-in members report a recovered, planned or not-found balloon from its flight page, in SondeHub's own format (serial, recovered by, recovery success, recovery planned, position, notes); it is sent to SondeHub and shown here

Chase mode on the Balloon Map for signed-in members: your position, the distance, bearing and directions to the balloon you pick, other chasers' cars, and an optional Share My Position that puts your car (CALLSIGN_chase) on SondeHub's map
New balloon icons for a planned recovery, a chase car and your own position; recovered, planned and not-found landings show on the map, with a Recovery filter and Hide recovered sondes

Settings > Map Areas: every map (home page, aircraft live map, Coverage Map, Balloon Map, Weather Map, County Map, Feeders map) has its own "opens on" area, all set to the whole of Arkansas by default
Read-only production access for troubleshooting (a locked-down key that can read logs and container state on the hub and nothing else; installed by you with one script)
improved: Backups: the restore screens have a Map Data area (hospitals, places, counties, air ambulances, interesting aircraft) and the balloon recovery reports; a test now fails if a table is in no area

The card beside the home map folds each block (Worth a Look, Records, The Network, Weather, Radiosondes) into a one-line headline you can open; it only scrolls once enough blocks are open, and it remembers which you opened
fixed: Browser location was blocked on every page by the site's security header; it is now allowed for this site only, so chase mode and Use Browser Position can ask for it
The Balloon Map, Weather Map and County Map open on Arkansas whole instead of fitting themselves to whatever balloons, stations or counties were loaded

title: Granular roles, one registry for every service, and a more consistent set of maps
added: Admin Feeders and MLAT lists have Actions (Manage, Details, Release, Assign, Ban) like the weather and radiosonde lists
Radiosonde receiving stations and balloon flights on the coverage map; every kind of point (hospitals, airports, stations, launch sites) can be switched on over the county map
Choose how precisely your station's location is shown: exact, within about 400 feet, 0.7 mile, 6 miles, 60 miles, or hidden

Granular administrator roles: separate permissions for weather stations, radiosondes and map data (and a repeater moderator, ready for the repeater directory); the broader Manage Feeders and Manage Settings still include them
Settings: Panels When a Map Opens. Every map now starts with its list, filters and legend closed (set it to Open to bring them back)

Home page: the map shows the balloon receiving stations and launch sites, and the card beside it has Weather Right Now and Radiosondes Right Now; the admin Overview has weather and radiosonde tiles, claims waiting and the launch-site and county data
improved: Menu: Places opens the County Map, and Weather lists Overview first and the Weather Map second, like Aircraft and Radiosondes
Clicking a marker on the county map or a county page opens the same popup as on the aircraft map (hospital, airport, station, balloon site) instead of jumping to another page

Stations that stand at the same place (an ADS-B feeder, a weather station, a balloon receiving station) no longer hide each other on the maps: their markers fan out around the shared spot, each still clickable

Administrators' Add forms for a member (weather station, feeder, radiosonde station) now offer every option the member has, find the member as you type (user name, display name, call sign or email) and can tie a weather station to one of the member's feeders
The county maps use the same airport, hospital and balloon icons as the other maps
County map hospitals show the heliport badge and link, and look faint when their position is only approximate, like the aircraft map
Menu entries and map behavior follow one rule on every map: the overview comes first and the map second, the same icons and popups, panels closed when a map opens
fixed: Update Now no longer leaves Grafana stuck when the update service and the stack updater replace the same container at once: the stack updater clears the container that holds the name and retries
Radiosonde receiving stations whose position was missing ("not known yet") get it back at once, from one request to SondeHub, instead of waiting for their next upload
Weather labels on the maps no longer cover a feeder at the same place: the label sits beside a small dot marking the station's position
The map on the home page can be zoomed: zoom buttons, double click and pinch always work, and the mouse wheel zooms once the map has been clicked

title: Weather balloons, the county map, and help for administrators
added: Copy buttons on code blocks and setup values (upload address, server, path, port, commands)
Radiosondes and balloons: National Weather Service balloons and amateur balloons over Arkansas and its neighbors, recorded live with their tracks, data and history
A Balloon Map in the same style as the aircraft map, flight pages with charts and a Skew-T diagram, launch sites and receiving stations, search, and CSV and GeoJSON downloads
Claim your radiosonde receiving station (by call sign, by a code in the station's antenna description, or approved by an administrator) and choose how its location is shown

County Map: every Arkansas county shaded by what is in it (feeders, weather stations, hospitals, airports, balloon launch sites), with a page for each county; counties are also layers on the aircraft map and the home map
Weather balloons card on the home page and a Weather balloons layer on the aircraft map
Weather balloon status: climbing (balloon intact) or burst and falling, recovery reports from SondeHub, balloon icons for launch, burst, falling and landing
Flight pages show the telemetry of the moment (updating by itself), and who is hearing the balloon with the signal now
Weather Statistics and Balloon Statistics dashboards in Grafana, and a hover read-out on the weather station charts
Radiosonde receiving stations are claimed for you automatically when their call sign (with or without a suffix such as -LR) matches your profile
Administrators can open and edit a member's weather station or radiosonde station with the member's own pages
Administrators can assign a radiosonde station to a member or start a claim for them
Administrators can add a weather station or an ADS-B feeder for a member, as well as assign a radiosonde station
improved: Weather setup pages now cover the Home Assistant (HACS) integration and a ready-made compose file for the Tempest bridge container
Am I Feeding? also checks your weather stations when you are signed in
Admin > Data Updates loads county outlines and balloon launch sites; Admin > Radiosondes shows the live feed and the claims
The Statistics Dashboard and Feeder Statistics pages are now called Aircraft Statistics and Aircraft Feeder Statistics
Bigger tap targets for airports, launch sites and stations on phones; Overview comes before the Balloon Map; the About page and the Roadmap's finished cards are up to date
Receiving Stations can be searched and sorted
Balloon icons can be resized and their labels turned off (hover shows the details); the balloon charts match the weather station charts, with icons
fixed: A duplicate navigation bar under the menu on the How to Feed pages is gone

Home Assistant setup no longer fails with 'Could not reach ArkSignal' for an http:// address (the site redirects to https; integration 1.0.2 follows it correctly), and the address shown for Home Assistant and scripts is the https one
Hospital position picker: Use the Picked Position now updates the Latitude and Longitude shown on the hospital
Receiving stations whose position was uploaded as text appeared at the wrong place (and so were missing from Arkansas)

title: Weather stations, a shared map look, Planefence speed-up
added: A Show on Map button on airport and hospital pages that opens the live map on that place

Weather stations: members' own stations (Ecowitt, Weather Underground format, Home Assistant, and Ecowitt.net accounts) with live conditions, charts, daily summaries, records, a map layer on the home and live maps, and a Weather card on the home page
Add a weather station to one of your ADS-B feeders, or run a weather-only station; choose public, approximate or hidden just like a feeder

Home Assistant users can install the ArkSignal Weather integration, pick their weather device and be done; a small Tempest bridge sends a Tempest station's own local readings without any cloud service (both are published separately)
A full Weather Map with radar and satellite layers, filters, wind arrows and a station list; weather stations on the aircraft map can show wind, temperature, rain and more
Condition icons (sunny, cloudy, rain, storm, wind, fog, night) and an icon for every reading on the weather station page
Plane-Alert can use your own Interesting Aircraft list as its alert list, so the list is kept in one place
Planefence now keeps low-flying aircraft only (up to 5,000 ft) after the first start of this release, so its list is much shorter; change it any time on Admin > Planefence
improved: In progress: the repeater directory
Buttons that ask for confirmation (such as Delete) now ask before they act on every page
Weather uploads accept values that carry their own unit, so any unit system works
Weather station charts are smaller and sit side by side
The weather map now has the same layout, layers, Weather panel and label choices as the aircraft map, with weather stations as labels that show a wind rose and any values you choose
Hospitals: setting or editing a position by hand takes the hospital off the review list, and the Address Lookup always has a map you can click to place the hospital when a lookup fails

The home page's right-now numbers, cards and map count only what is in Arkansas (a margin of 15 miles), so a station or aircraft far away or across the border does not skew them; it can be switched off in Settings
Planefence and Plane-Alert load faster: the aircraft list now streams to the page as it is read instead of being collected first, pages are compressed (about a fifth of the size) and cached briefly
fixed: Flight paths: a flight that lands out of range and flies again hours later is now drawn as a separate leg instead of joined to the earlier one by a straight line
The phone menu shows each group name and its arrow on one line
After saving something on a page (such as Use This Position on a hospital) the page no longer jumps to the top: the confirmation stays in view where you are
Weather stations now show on the coverage map, with their own layer

title: Hospital checks, our own address search, a real admin overview and a calmer layout
added: Admin > Hospitals: Import Hospital Data (renamed from Import Trauma Levels) now also understands the capability tags surgeon, trauma ICU, CT, vascular, interventional radiology, facial and eye injuries; a file adds to the services on record and never removes one

Admin > Hospitals: an Address Lookup on every hospital (pre-filled with its address) asks the US Census, our own Photon address search and OpenStreetMap, lists the answers with a small map, and Use This Position keeps the one you choose
Admin > Interesting Aircraft: our own editable list that feeds the Interesting flag on the live map, with a CSV import, the Plane-Alert database (by category) and a Data Updates job
Our own address search (Photon, US data from OpenStreetMap) joins the stack and installs itself with Update Now

Admin > Hospitals: Check All Positions looks up every hospital's address with the Census and our own Photon, confirms the position where they agree and lists the rest for review; Check This Position does one hospital at once

Admin > Hospitals: Data Issues flags hospitals with a missing or incomplete address, an approximate position, no phone number, a trauma centre with no heliport, or a heliport that is far from its hospital or not in the airport data, with a filter for each
Live map: the Filters and Weather panels fold up from a small arrow on their bottom edge, and the choice is remembered
Live map: the altitude colour scale now stays under the map at all times, in your chosen units
Menu: Airports and Hospitals now sit in their own Places group instead of under Aircraft

Service Status now lists the address search (Photon), Planefence, and every outside data source we use (OurAirports, the Census, the hospital list, the aircraft databases, weather, photos, routes, map tiles and layers) with whether it is answering and when our copy was last refreshed
Admin Overview is now a real overview: what needs attention with a link to fix each thing, the network at a glance, the data we keep, the services behind the site and recent activity
A Map button in the top bar, next to Display, opens the live map from any page (on a phone it stays beside the menu button)

Page width: on very wide monitors page content is limited to a comfortable width and centred (maps still use the whole window). Choose Full width in the Display menu or on your profile page; the site default and the limit are settings
improved: Settings: the long Maps and Data Sources section is split into Map Tiles and Weather, Hospitals, Air Ambulance, Interesting Aircraft, Places and Search and Address Finders, under a new Facilities and Lookups tab
Admin menu: the pages are grouped (People, Network, Map and Data, Site, System) and always in the same order
Distance settings are now shown and typed in feet and miles by default, with metres and kilometres one setting away; a unit typed with a number (250 m, 0.5 mi) is understood either way
Dropdown menus stand out more: a lighter surface, an accent edge and a shadow, with the page behind them stepping back

Home page: a taller map that always shows the whole of Arkansas, with every kind of station on it (switchable in a legend), and a live Right Now panel (emergencies, air ambulances, military and listed aircraft, records, network activity) instead of the release notes
Flight page: the map now fills its section
Live map: the Legend is now a button in the top row next to Weather and Filters and opens as a panel under them, instead of a box floating at the bottom
Every section on a page is the same width, on wide screens and on phones
fixed: Admin > Hospitals: the Import button always did a preview; it now imports
Hospital positions you confirm or set by hand are no longer overwritten by hospital list updates
Hospitals list: the Trauma column no longer wraps (Level IV broke onto two lines), and sorting by it puts the levels in order I to V with hospitals that have none last

Aircraft Tracking: the radar is no longer huge; it scales with the window (never more than about 680 pixels), the number cards are compact, and a list of the highest aircraft in the air fills the space beside the radar
Settings: saving the whole Settings form no longer changes the distance settings that were not part of it

title: Fixed-wing air ambulances, a site icon and fixes
added: A site icon: a signal-arc badge in the browser tab, on bookmarks, as a phone home-screen icon and in the web app manifest

Fixed-wing air ambulances and medical transports (Pilatus PC-12, King Air, small jets) beside the helicopters: found from the aircraft database by owner names set in Settings, plus tail numbers you add as fixed wing; a second Aircraft Flags entry, Air ambulance (fixed wing), and the aircraft card says which kind it is
fixed: The Admin > Updates page title no longer shows page code in the browser tab, and its Live Content settings section (the source of the live Release Notes and Roadmap) is back on the page; it had slipped into the title

title: Complete feed pages, hospital filters and positions, Data Updates and consistent names
added: Admin > Hospitals can ask OpenStreetMap where a hospital with only an approximate position is, one at a time or twelve at a time, and keeps the answer

Admin > Data Updates: one page with a schedule for every outside data set (places, airports, hospitals, trauma levels and services, air ambulances), a Run Now button, the last result and the next run, one time of day for all, and failures shown on Status. A source that fails keeps its last good data and tries again later. Trauma levels and services can be read automatically from the address of a CSV file kept by the trauma system
improved: The How to Feed pages are complete and consistent: ADS-B, MLAT and UAT each have How It Works, What You Need, Hardware, Hardware Setup, Software Setup, After You Are Feeding, Ports, Troubleshooting, Your Data and More Help, and point to each other (ADS-B and MLAT usually run together)
Air ambulance moved to Aircraft Flags (it is a property of an aircraft, not a type), and Military is offered once, under Aircraft Flags, instead of twice

Hospital positions are better: a second try with the street written other ways, then the hospital's own helipad from the airport data, then the trauma list's coordinates; hospitals guessed at the same place are spread out so none hides another; hospital names keep CHI, VA and LLC in capitals
In progress: fixed-wing air ambulances

title: ArkSignal: new name, home page, menus, hospitals, air ambulances and more
added: Coverage Map (/coverage): one map with a layer for each kind of service: ADS-B coverage around every station, MLAT stations, and UAT / ADS-R traffic right now. More layers join it as the network grows
Choose the page you land on after signing in (Profile > After I sign in, take me to), with a site default set by an administrator in Settings > Accounts. A page you were heading to still wins
The How to Feed section is split into pages with a sub-menu: ADS-B, MLAT, UAT (978 MHz) and Am I Feeding?. Old links keep working
Settings are grouped into tabs (General, Accounts and Security, Map and Data, Feeders and Alerts, Updates and Backups) with a search box that finds a setting by name

The network is now called ArkSignal. The header wordmark, page titles (Page | ArkSignal), About, emails and the Feed and Support wording follow it; the name, accent part and tagline are settings (Admin > Settings > General), and adsb.allisononline.org keeps working
A rewritten About page: what the network is, who runs it (a hobby project run by two volunteers), what you can do here today, where it is going, and credits for the MLAT server, Planefence and rclone

A new home page: ArkSignal at a glance, with a live strip (aircraft overhead, stations online, MLAT, service status), a map preview, one search box for a callsign, tail number, airport, city or station, a card for each service and the latest release. The previous home page is now Aircraft Tracking (/aircraft, also in the menu)

Moving to arksignal.allisononline.org: an administrator can set a Main Address and a list of Old Addresses (Settings > General) so page requests on the old address are sent to the new one with a permanent redirect; it stays off until it is filled in

Search the live map by place: type a city, ZIP code or county in the map search box and pick it from the list (or press Enter) to jump there. The places come from the US Census Bureau and are loaded by an administrator under Admin > Places

Hospitals: a public Hospitals list and a page for each hospital (address, emergency care, trauma level and services where known, and the heliport it uses), a Hospitals layer on the live map coloured by trauma level, and an Admin > Hospitals page that loads the list from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and finds each hospital with the Census Bureau geocoder. Trauma levels, services and heliport links are entered by an administrator and kept by every update

Air ambulance helicopters: an Air ambulance entry in the live map's Aircraft Type filter (count, chip, and a line on the aircraft card naming the operator). They are found from the aircraft database tar1090 uses (helicopters owned by Air Evac, Air Methods, Med-Trans, Life Flight Network, REACH, hospitals and similar) plus a tail number list an administrator keeps in Admin > Air Ambulance

Import trauma levels: Admin > Hospitals takes a CSV list of trauma-designated hospitals (with a preview), matches it to the hospitals by position and name, adds the ones the public list lacks, and shows the level, designation date and source on each hospital page
A map legend on the live map: a collapsible panel that explains the colours of whatever layers are switched on

Administrators can open any account (Admin > Users, click a name) and change what the person can change themselves: email address, display name, callsign, display choices and landing page, alert webhook and alert rules, and sign-ins, with two-factor reset, a temporary password and unlock. The current password is never shown to anyone, only replaced; every change is written to the audit log, and only a Super Admin can change a Super Admin

Hospital filters: choose which kinds of facility are loaded (acute care, critical access, children's, rural emergency, Veterans Administration, Department of Defense, psychiatric, long-term), leave out names containing words such as BEHAVIORAL or SURGICAL, and optionally keep only hospitals with an emergency department. Behavioral health centres are out by default, and an update removes loaded facilities that no longer match (anything edited by hand is kept)

Hospital services: stroke, neurosurgery, cardiac, obstetrics, NICU, children's, burn, orthopedics, cancer and psychiatric tags on hospitals, a Service filter on the Hospitals list, and a CSV import that can carry them (with the CMS number for exact matching). The hospital import now keeps only hospitals with an emergency department by default
improved: The top menu and a slim bottom bar (About, Status, Release Notes, Roadmap, Contact) stay in view while you scroll long pages, on phones too
Search boxes on the admin Users, Feeders, MLAT and Map Layers lists, and on the public Feeders page; click a column heading to sort
Flights, Flight History and Airports can be sorted by any column
New stations are shown feed.arksignal.allisononline.org on the How to Feed page; stations already using feed.adsb.allisononline.org keep working and the page says so

The top menu is grouped by service: Aircraft (map, flights, history, airports, MLAT, tools), Network (coverage, stations, statistics, status) and Feed, with the part of the site you are in highlighted; new services get their own group as they arrive

Inside Aircraft, Network or Feed a second bar under the top menu lists that service's pages with the current one marked; clicking a group name goes to that section, and resting the mouse on it opens its menu
Live map: every filter that is on shows as a small chip you can click to switch it off, with a Clear All button
The top menu and the section bar now run the full width of the window and fold into a menu button on narrow screens instead of being cut off

Hospitals on the live map are square badges instead of dots: the trauma level number on a colour for trauma centres, a red plus for an emergency department, grey for none, and a blue H where a heliport is linked, so they stand apart from airports
Airport weather on the live map now refreshes by itself every few minutes (the weather refresh setting) instead of only when the map is moved

adsb.allisononline.org now sends visitors to arksignal.allisononline.org (page requests only; the feed and MLAT addresses are untouched). The Main Address and the list of old addresses are in Settings > General
fixed: Hospital markers on the live map can be clicked, like the airports
The admin user page uses one consistent width and shows the user name as plain text

title: Planefence, off-site backups, live release notes and roadmap
added: Planefence and Plane-Alert: which aircraft flew over Arkansas, with photos, airlines and routes, and a list of interesting aircraft (military, government, rare); in the Tools menu, with notifications (Discord, Mastodon and others) set up on an administrator-only configuration page. It arrives with Update Now, with no files to edit by hand

Off-site backups: Admin > Backups > Off-Site Copy sends encrypted copies of everything (the portal database with all flights and history, the hub's secret keys and settings, Grafana, statistics history and the hub's traffic history) to an SFTP server, S3 bucket, NAS share or WebDAV, with a small daily copy and a big weekly copy as separate files, connection test, copy-now buttons and a history of runs

Restore Part: restore only some areas of a backup (accounts, stations, flight history, alerts, settings...), or bring back one person, station, role or alert rule with what belongs to it, in merge or replace mode, with a safety backup first. The off-site restore helper can also unpack only chosen parts
Aircraft Type filter on the live map: helicopters, jets, turboprops, piston props, large and heavy, light aircraft, gliders and balloons, drones, ground vehicles and unknown type, with counts
A public Roadmap page (/roadmap): what is coming next, in progress, planned and just released, filterable by area

Live Release Notes and Roadmap: both pages read their lists from the project's repository, so they update as soon as work is pushed instead of staying frozen at the last release (Admin > Updates > Live Content)

A Support page (hidden until an administrator sets it up in Admin > Support): why donations help, what the network costs to run with a monthly progress bar, links to Ko-fi and PayPal, and an Equipment Fund wish list for antennas, receivers and mesh nodes the project installs at host sites. The portal only links out and never handles payment details
improved: The keyboard shortcuts help opens as a popup in the middle of the screen, on top of everything
Registration, change password, reset and forgot-password forms list their requirements and tick them as you type, including user name rules, email format and whether the two passwords match

Every section of the live map's filters (Stations, Show, Data Source, Aircraft Flags, Aircraft Type, Altitude, Display and View, Layers) folds up like the sections of the aircraft details card, remembers whether you left it open, and shows a small count of the filters active in it
fixed: Am I Feeding said MLAT was not connected for a claimed station even when it was working

Units on the live map: aeronautical (ft, kt, nm), metric or imperial, chosen per visitor with a site default in Settings
Keyboard shortcuts on the live map with the same keys as tar1090 (F, I, U, V, L, O, K, B, R, H, Q, E, arrows, / and ?), plus a help panel
Search on the live map takes several terms with commas, * wildcards and ! to leave terms out, and also matches squawk and model
Aircraft Flags filter (military, interesting, PIA, LADD) in the live map's filter card

Links to a view: the live map reads position, zoom, filters, units and the selected aircraft from the address, and Copy Link to This View builds one
Altitude chart and Export KML on the aircraft details card
Wide / Narrow button for the details card, a hover block on aircraft, a geometric-altitude label field and Reset My Map Settings
This Release Notes page
improved: Admin > Status says why a service failed, and its overall banner counts every row

Data Source filter and the aircraft card treat UAT and ADS-R as one source, as the hub reports them
fixed: The stack updater clears a leftover parked container and retries, which fixes the 'portal FAILED' row on Admin > Status

title: MLAT everywhere, service status, new feed page

MLAT status in plain words on My Station (with what to fix), the public Feeders list and station pages, the public API, the feed check and the admin pages

Data Source filter on the live map (ADS-B, MLAT, UAT/ADS-R, TIS-B, Mode S, other) with live counts

improved: The How to Feed page was rewritten: how ADS-B, MLAT and UAT work, setup for new and existing stations, ports, troubleshooting and privacy
Nginx Proxy Manager is told to reload after any service is replaced, so a replaced container is never answered with a stale address

Flight Progress draws the right aircraft shape for each type instead of one generic icon

fixed: Sky View no longer steps backward between position reports
